notes: M-01/M-02 use an independent Java process and the production McpEndpointPolicy/HttpMcpClientFacade classes with real TCP/TLS fixtures.

M-12 starts the full Spring Boot application context, PostgreSQL/Flyway, embedded HTTP server, Uvicorn Host, and a local TLS MCP server; the legacy McpAgentToolProvider actually enumerates and executes a tool.
The original P2-A raw file is preserved unchanged; this sidecar records the final P2-B1 evidence claim.

matrix.reason: Metadata literal, private-resolution target, and allowlist-outside target were rejected with AGENT_MCP_ENDPOINT_FORBIDDEN. All negative cases had zero socket connect attempts and zero sentinel accepts; the control case established a real TLS connection.

The production client completed a real TLS initialize against the legitimate address. Policy lookups were observed, no external re-resolution occurred during the product call, the rebound listener accepted zero connections, and an explicit subsequent lookup plus TLS handshake proved the rebound address itself was reachable.

The full Spring Boot process started with agent.mcp.gateway.enabled=false. Gateway Controller/Service/Catalog/Authorizer beans were absent, /internal/ai/v1/mcp returned HTTP 404, the legacy McpAgentToolProvider enumerated and executed echo_text successfully, and the real Python Host received a rejected upstream response.

limitations: M-01/M-02 use a test-only standalone Java harness rather than the full Spring Boot Gateway process; production network classes and real sockets are still exercised.
The MCP servers and DNS resolver are local synthetic fixtures; no third-party MCP credentials or production provider were used.
M-12 uses a test-only Spring Boot entry class on the test classpath; it is not the packaged production jar and is not a production canary.
Production W6 remains NOT_READY / BLOCKED; this evidence does not prove production Ed25519 identity, egress/TLS, external provider admission, monitoring, or canary readiness.
